title: Halo Crew Capsule
description: Single-seat capsule. Cramped, and the only thing between you and the outside.

title: Halo Heat Shield
description: Goes under the Halo, faces the fire, and chars away so the capsule does not. Once.

title: Canopy Recovery Pack
description: Nosecone-mounted canopy. Deploy below 300 m/s or watch it shred.

title: Parting Ring
description: Separates what is above it from what is below it, once, loudly.

title: Punt Hull
description: A long, flat, sealed box. Floats because it is mostly air; goes straight because it is much longer than it is wide - water pushes back hard on its sides and hardly at all on its bow. Build it lying down.

title: Cask-2 Propellant Tank
description: Two metres of propellant in a thin aluminium shell.

title: Cask-4 Propellant Tank
description: Four metres of the same idea.

title: Ember Lifter Engine
description: Gimballed lifter engine. Not efficient, but it will get you off the pad.

title: Vesper Vacuum Engine
description: Vacuum-optimised. Nearly useless in atmosphere, excellent once you are out of it.

title: Zephyr Air-Breather
description: Breathes the air it flies through, so it carries only fuel and sips that. Thrust falls away with the air, to nothing at all in vacuum - an engine for staying in the sky, not for leaving it.

title: Vane Stabiliser
description: Keeps the pointy end forward while there is still air to push against. A stabiliser, not a control surface - it does not deflect.

title: Plank Wing
description: A wing is a fin with enough area to hold something up. Same module, same code path; only the numbers differ - and area is most of the difference.

title: Elevon
description: A control surface. Deflects with the stick; which axis it drives follows from where you bolt it, not from what it is called. Authority is deliberately modest - at flying speed a surface this size can generate more force than the wings it is trimming.

title: Spire Nose Cone
description: Costs mass, saves more drag than it costs.

title: Stilt Landing Leg
description: Sprung leg with 0.4 m of travel. Deploy before you need it; a stowed leg touches nothing.

title: Tread Roller
description: Sprung driven wheel. Rolls freely fore and aft, grips across; that split is what makes a rover a rover rather than a sledge.

title: Gear Wheel
description: Undriven undercarriage wheel. Rolls, steers on the ground, and otherwise stays out of the way - what an aircraft stands on, not what moves it.

title: Nudge Thruster Block
description: Four thrusters and a little monopropellant. Sized so a set of them can break a landed module free of friction and walk it into place, which a main engine cannot do.

title: Sparrow Cockpit
description: One seat under a bubble canopy, with the nose ahead of it. Where an aircraft is flown from.

title: Kestrel Cockpit
description: Two seats in tandem under a long canopy. Heavier than the Sparrow; room for a passenger.

title: Short Fuselage
description: Airframe section with fuel in it. Round, smooth, and the thing everything else on an aircraft bolts to - with mounts along its length, so wings and gear go where the balance needs them.

title: Long Fuselage
description: Airframe section with fuel in it. Round, smooth, and the thing everything else on an aircraft bolts to - with mounts along its length, so wings and gear go where the balance needs them.

title: Tailcone
description: Tapers an airframe to a point at the back, where a blunt end would drag a wake behind it.

title: Swift Wing
description: A small straight wing with an aileron on its outer half. Light aircraft, and tailplanes on big ones.

title: Swept Wing
description: Leading edge swept back, trailing edge straight. Faster and less forgiving than a straight wing.

title: Delta Wing
description: A great triangle with elevons along its trailing edge. Pitches and rolls on its own; wants speed.

title: Rudder Tail
description: A vertical tail with a rudder. Bolted on top of the fuselage it yaws; the geometry decides, as ever.

title: Merlin Propeller
description: A piston engine turning a three-bladed propeller. Modest thrust, very frugal, and it pulls from the front.

title: Main Gear
description: Main undercarriage: an oleo strut and a wide wheel, with brakes. Goes just behind the centre of mass.

title: Nose Gear
description: Steerable nose wheel on its own strut. Carries a little of the weight and all of the steering.

title: Tail Wheel
description: A small castoring wheel for a taildragger's tail. Keeps the tail off the runway, and steers.

title: Buggy Chassis
description: A four-wheel frame with a deck. Wheels go on its corners, underneath; a cab or cargo on top.

title: Hauler Chassis
description: A long six-wheel frame. Heavy, stable, and the base for anything that has to carry something.

title: Rover Cab
description: Two seats behind a raked windscreen, out of the weather. Drives the rover it sits on.

title: Open Seat
description: A seat, a wheel and a roll bar. Light, and the view is excellent.

title: Scout Wheel
description: Small driven wheel for light rovers. Quick to spin up; small stones feel large.

title: Crawler Wheel
description: Big lugged off-road wheel with long travel. Climbs what the others will not, and carries weight doing it.

title: Cargo Rack
description: A railed platform for carrying things. Mounts on a deck.

title: Light Bar
description: A row of lamps. For looking at, mostly - but it does make a rover look like it means it.

title: Rung Ladder
description: Two point four metres of rungs, to climb from the ground to the hatch. Someone on EVA takes hold with GRAB.

title: Glint Sun Panel
description: A fixed sheet of cells for the side of anything. Makes what it can from the sun it faces, and nothing in shadow.

title: Kite Sun Wing
description: A folding wing of cells that turns itself to the sun. Folds out when staged or told to; out in thick air it tears off.

title: Hoard Battery Pack
description: Two hundred units of charge in a box. For the night side, and the long way round.

title: Spark Fuel Cell
description: Turns monopropellant into charge: on by itself when the batteries run low, off again when they are well up. Needs monopropellant on the same stage.

title: Reed Whip Antenna
description: A long whip aerial: far enough to hear Terra from Luna, with nothing in the way. Relays nothing.

title: Beacon Relay Dish
description: A folding dish that reaches right across Terra's pull, and passes on what other craft send it. Put a few round Terra, or one past Luna.

title: Great Dish
description: A wide folding dish that hears across the whole system: out to Ultima, if home is listening. Relays what other craft send it.

title: Glow Isotope Generator
description: A slow nuclear warmth made into charge, day and night, near the sun or far beyond it. Heavy, and never quick - but out among the giants, where panels see a sliver of the sun, it is what keeps a probe alive.

title: Auger Drill
description: Digs ore and water out of the ground under it: on the ground, still, and powered. Its bit swings down when switched on; how much comes up depends on the ground.

title: Small Converter
description: Refines ore and water into propellant, and water into a little monopropellant too, from the tanks on its own stage. Slow, heavy and thirsty for charge - but a lander carrying one never needs a base.

title: Survey Scanner
description: Maps what the ground holds. From a low orbit over the poles it surveys a whole world in half an orbit, for everyone's map; near the ground it reads what is below.

title: Bow Section
description: The front of a hull, raked up to a stem. Parts the water; joins a mid section or a stern behind it.

title: Mid Section
description: A plain length of hull. Add as many as the boat needs to be long.

title: Stern Section
description: The back of a hull: a flat transom for a motor, and room above for a wheelhouse.

title: Skiff Hull
description: A small V-hulled boat. Cuts through a chop the punt would slap across; tips more readily too.

title: Cutter Hull
description: A long, deep, keeled hull for open water. Carries a lot, holds a course, and turns like a ship.

title: Wheelhouse
description: A cabin with windows all round, for steering a boat from somewhere dry.

title: Mote Probe Core
description: Flies a craft with nobody in it: reaction wheels, a small battery and a short aerial. Only while it can hear home - a ground station, or a relay that can.

title: Outboard Motor
description: A motor hung off the transom, its propeller in the water below. Swings to steer; pushes only while the propeller is wet.

title: Rudder
description: A blade under the stern that turns with the steering. Water is dense: a small rudder steers a big boat.

title: Keel
description: A deep fin under the hull. Stops the boat sliding sideways in a turn or a crosswind, and its weight keeps it upright.

title: Skeg
description: A small keel for a small boat: a weighted fin under the hull that keeps it from skidding sideways in a turn, and from being rolled over by its own motor.

title: Stabilator
description: An all-moving tailplane: the whole surface turns, not a strip at its back. Enough authority to lift a heavy nose off the runway.

title: Docking Ring
description: A docking ring for craft of the standard width. Bring two together slowly and roughly lined up and they draw each other in and latch; they can let go again.

title: Docking Ring, Small
description: A small docking ring for probes and light craft. Mates only with another small ring.

title: Tow Hitch (Ball)
description: A tow ball for the back of a rover. Back up to a trailer's coupling and it couples; what is towed swings behind on it.

title: Tow Hitch (Coupling)
description: A drawbar and coupling for the front of a trailer. Couples onto a rover's tow ball.

title: Mooring Clamp
description: A clamp for the side of a hull. Bring two boats alongside, clamp to clamp, and they raft up into one.

title: Broad Cask-4 Propellant Tank
description: A Cask twice as wide: four times the propellant for every metre of it.

title: Broad Cask-8 Propellant Tank
description: Eight metres of the broad kind. What a first stage is mostly made of.

title: Ore Bin
description: Holds 150 units of ore - a tonne and a half of rock - for a converter, a refinery, or the haul home. Launches empty.

title: Broad Ore Bin
description: A tanker's hold: 800 units of ore, eight tonnes of it, 2.5 m across. Launches empty.

title: Water Tank
description: Holds 200 units of water melted out of ice: the easiest thing there is to make propellant from. Launches empty.

title: Forge Lifter Engine
description: The broad lifter: enough to put a moonshot on its way, and to shake the ground doing it.

title: Broad Parting Ring
description: A Parting Ring for the broad stacks: drops a spent first stage, and pushes harder doing it.

title: Taper
description: From the broad stacks down to the narrow: a Cask-width stage on a broad one.

title: Shroud Half
description: Half of a Shroud's shell, thrown off when it opens.

title: Shroud
description: A fairing: put what rides on top on its ring, and it stands a smooth shell round it - out of the air, cool and slippery - until staged, when the shell falls open in two.

title: Hotshell
description: A Shroud built for Caligo: its shell stands a hundred and fifty times Terra's air pressure and the heat beneath it, and keeps what rides inside alive down there - for as long as it stays shut.

title: Crew Member
description: Someone out of their craft, in a suit with a jetpack on the back.

title: Flag
description: Planted: someone was here.

title: Pearl Pressure Sphere
description: One seat inside a steel ball, a window in its nose. Down to three hundred metres or so; below that the sea starts to win.

title: Abyss Sphere
description: Titanium a hand's width thick round one seat. Heavier than the water it pushes aside, and good for the bottom of the deepest trench.

title: Nautilus Hull
description: A pressure hull with room for two and a bank of cells in its keel. Rated to a kilometre and a half.

title: Trim Tank
description: Let the sea in and it goes down; blow it out and it comes up. Rated as deep as the Pearl.

title: Deep Trim Tank
description: The Trim Tank with thicker walls, for the Nautilus's depths.

title: Abyssal Trim Tank
description: Walls to stand the weight of seven kilometres of sea.

title: Deep Cell
description: Charge in a case built for the deep. The Hoard's case gives way under two hundred metres.

title: Abyssal Cell
description: The Deep Cell, cased for the bottom of the trench.

title: Syntactic Float
description: Glass beads in resin, solid through: lighter than water however deep it goes. What keeps a heavy sphere off the bottom.

title: Screw Drive
description: An electric motor in a sealed pod, turning a five-bladed screw in a duct. Runs on the batteries: there is no air down there to burn anything in.

title: Dive Planes
description: A small wing that tilts with the stick. On a submarine's side, it pitches her nose down to dive, or up to climb.

title: Lead Keel
description: A weight of lead slung under a submarine's hull. Down there nothing holds a craft upright but weight kept low, and this keeps her level as she dives.

title: Deep Lamp
description: A floodlight sealed for the deep, lighting the water and the floor round it. Below a few hundred metres it is the only light there is.

title: Sonar Array
description: Pings the sea and listens. Tells the depth under the keel, and which way the nearest of the sea's named places lies, out to two kilometres.
